technical_core.canonical_statement: A scalar is a physical quantity completely specified by a single real number representing magnitude with appropriate units, obeying ordinary algebra.
technical_core.why_required: Prevents treating scalar quantities as directed entities.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Learner adds mass, speed, or time vectorially.

technical_core.canonical_statement: A vector is a physical quantity possessing both a non-negative magnitude and an intrinsic spatial direction that transforms according to vector algebra.
technical_core.why_required: Establishes that having direction alone is insufficient (e.g. electric current is scalar).
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Misconception that current or pressure is a vector.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Vectors are denoted by an arrow over a symbol or boldface; magnitude is denoted by |A| or A, with |A| >= 0.
technical_core.why_required: Distinguishes vector state from scalar magnitude.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Equations conflating vector with magnitude.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Direction in a 2D plane is specified relative to a declared reference axis (standard: CCW from +x axis).
technical_core.why_required: Magnitude without directional reference is incomplete.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Ambiguous vectors floating without coordinate orientation.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Two vectors are equal iff their magnitudes and directions are identical, independent of spatial origin (free vectors).
technical_core.why_required: Enables parallel transport for geometric addition.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Inability to translate vectors geometrically.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: A is vector, |A| is non-negative scalar magnitude

representations.name: Vector Arrow Diagram
representations.physics_encoded: Directed line segment representing magnitude (length) and planar orientation (arrowhead)
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Explicit arrowhead and declared reference line
representations.common_incorrect_version: Arrow drawn floating in space with angle marked but no reference axis
representations.verification_method: Check invariance of vector under reference frame rotation

model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Curved parallel transport requires Riemannian geometry
Bound vectors cannot be freely translated

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Identify physical quantity and discriminate scalar vs vector
Establish reference axis and origin
Extract magnitude (A >= 0) and measure angle relative to declared axis
Apply formal vector notation (|A| vs A)

required_transformations.description: Wind at 20 m/s North-East -> (|v|=20 m/s, theta=45 deg N of E)
(50 N, 120 deg) -> scaled directed line segment

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Any physical quantity with magnitude and direction is a vector
misconceptions.why_plausible: Current in a wire has an arrowhead indicating direction
misconceptions.required_counterexample: Current at a wire junction adds algebraically (I1+I2=I3), not vectorially
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Vector must obey vector addition laws and transform correctly under spatial rotation

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: A negative vector has a negative magnitude
misconceptions.required_counterexample: -A has magnitude |-A| = |A| >= 0; minus sign reverses direction
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Enforce |A| >= 0 unconditionally; minus sign represents 180 deg direction flip

problem_families.name: Polar Vector Specification
problem_families.recognition_cues: Word problem specifying quantity, unit, and geographic or planar heading
problem_families.first_technical_move: Draw Cartesian axes and fix positive angle baseline
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Drawing arrow from origin without declaring reference axis
problem_families.typical_unknown: Polar tuple (r, theta) and scaled arrow

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Basic definitions, scalar/vector discrimination, polar baseline translation

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Omitting scalar vs vector distinction and magnitude positivity
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Scalar vs vector distinction must be explicit and |A| >= 0 enforced

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Vector Addition, Subtraction, and the Resultant

technical_core.canonical_statement: The resultant vector R = A + B is the single vector that produces the identical physical effect as the individual vectors combined.
technical_core.why_required: Anchors physical equivalence of combined vectors.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Learner computes magnitude without understanding physical equivalence.

technical_core.canonical_statement: If two vectors are drawn head-to-tail, the third side from initial tail to final head is their resultant.
technical_core.why_required: Primary operational definition of vector addition.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Adding vectors tail-to-tail without parallel transport.

technical_core.canonical_statement: If two concurrent vectors are drawn tail-to-tail, the diagonal of the completed parallelogram from the common tail is the resultant.
technical_core.why_required: Standard construction for concurrent forces at an origin.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Inability to find resultant of concurrent forces.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Vector subtraction is defined as adding the negative vector: A - B = A + (-B).
technical_core.why_required: Enforces consistency with change in velocity and relative motion.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Subtracting magnitudes directly (|A - B| = A - B).

technical_core.canonical_statement: The zero vector has zero magnitude and indeterminate direction; A + (-A) = 0.
technical_core.why_required: Closes vector algebra under subtraction and equilibrium.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Treating vector zero as a scalar without directional dimensionality.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: R: resultant magnitude, A,B: vector magnitudes, theta: included angle tail-to-tail
alpha: angle of resultant R relative to vector A

representations.name: Head-to-Tail Triangle
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Directional arrowheads and resultant pointing from first tail to final head
representations.common_incorrect_version: Resultant drawn head-to-head forming a continuous cyclic loop summing to zero
representations.verification_method: Trace path along arrows: resultant must bridge start to finish directly

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Verify dimensional compatibility of vectors
Draw vectors tail-to-tail to identify true angle theta
Construct head-to-tail triangle or parallelogram
Draw resultant from first tail to final head
Apply R = sqrt(A^2 + B^2 + 2AB cos theta)
Calculate directional angle alpha relative to baseline vector
Check limiting collinear cases (theta = 0, 90, 180 deg)

required_transformations.description: Walk 3 m East then 4 m North -> Right triangle with hypotenuse 5 m

misconceptions.required_counterexample: 3 N East + 4 N West = 1 N East; only equals 7 N when collinear theta = 0
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Enforce triangle inequality: |A - B| <= R <= A + B

misconceptions.required_counterexample: If A is 5 m/s East and B is 5 m/s North, |A - B| = 5*sqrt(2) m/s != 0
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Invert B to -B then add vectorially

problem_families.name: Two-Vector Resultant
problem_families.recognition_cues: Two vectors with known magnitudes and included angle
problem_families.first_technical_move: Draw vectors tail-to-tail to confirm angle theta
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Using supplementary angle instead of interior angle
problem_families.typical_unknown: Resultant R and direction angle alpha

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Trigonometric law of cosines, directional angle determination, scalar sum misconceptions

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Cyclic loop head-to-tail drawn and stated as resultant
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Cyclic head-to-tail loop sums to zero, inverts resultant direction

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Parallelogram formula presented without limiting collinear checks
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Collinear checks theta=0, 90, 180 deg are mandatory

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Resolution of Vectors into Orthogonal Components

technical_core.canonical_statement: Any vector in a 2D plane can be uniquely decomposed into two perpendicular projections along orthogonal axes: A = A_x i + A_y j.
technical_core.why_required: Converts 2D spatial problems into two decoupled 1D scalar problems.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Learner attempts 2D dynamics without resolving along motion axes.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Dimensionless vectors of unit magnitude (i, j, k) specifying spatial axis directions.
technical_core.why_required: Separates magnitude from directional axis notation.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Writing vector sums as bare scalars.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Scalar components A_x and A_y are signed real numbers depending on alignment with declared positive axes.
technical_core.why_required: 1D vector directions are encoded purely by algebraic signs (+/-).
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Dropping signs and treating components as purely positive magnitudes.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Given orthogonal components, original vector is recovered via A = sqrt(A_x^2 + A_y^2) and theta = atan2(A_y, A_x).
technical_core.why_required: Completes bi-directional translation Vector <-> Components.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Authoring teaches decomposition but leaves learner unable to state final vector.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Orthogonal vector components are mutually independent; variation along x has zero influence along y.
technical_core.why_required: Foundational for 2D kinematics and Newton's second law axis decoupling.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Mixing horizontal forces into vertical acceleration equations.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: A_x: horizontal component, theta: angle from adjacent x-axis
mandatory_equations.reference_frame_or_sign: Cartesian frame; sign depends on quadrant

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: A_y: vertical component, theta: angle from adjacent x-axis
mandatory_equations.reference_frame_or_sign: Cartesian frame; sign depends on quadrant

representations.name: Component Right Triangle
representations.physics_encoded: Vector as hypotenuse of right triangle formed by orthogonal components
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Explicit right-angle square marker and clear adjacent axis for angle
representations.common_incorrect_version: Drawing components without arrowheads or swapping sin and cos when angle is vertical
representations.verification_method: Check Pythagorean consistency: sqrt(A_x^2 + A_y^2) == A

model_conditions.why_needed: Ensures independence of components without cross-terms
model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Oblique axes require metric tensor components

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Fix coordinate system and orientation of +x and +y
Identify angle theta and mark which axis is adjacent
Resolve components: adjacent = A*cos(theta), opposite = A*sin(theta)
Assign explicit algebraic signs (+/-) based on quadrant
Write vector in unit-vector basis: A = A_x i + A_y j
Reconstruct resultant magnitude and quadrant angle

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: A_x is ALWAYS A*cos(theta) and A_y is ALWAYS A*sin(theta)
misconceptions.why_plausible: Introductory textbook examples always measure angles from the horizontal
misconceptions.required_counterexample: On an incline, angle with normal is theta, so F_gy = mg*cos(theta) and F_gx = mg*sin(theta)
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Adjacent component uses cos(theta); opposite component uses sin(theta)

problem_families.name: Orthogonal Vector Resolution
problem_families.recognition_cues: Vector at arbitrary angle requiring rectangular components
problem_families.first_technical_move: Mark angle and identify adjacent vs opposite axes
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Blindly writing A_x = A*cos(theta) when angle is with vertical

problem_families.name: Polar Vector Recovery
problem_families.first_technical_move: Plot components on Cartesian grid to identify quadrant
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Ignoring signs and computing bare arctan(|A_y/A_x|)
problem_families.typical_unknown: Magnitude A and true heading theta

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: High quadrant sign sensitivity, adjacent vs opposite angle traps, resultant reconstruction

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Component resolution taught without coordinate axes or sign conventions
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Sign convention and coordinate axes are mandatory for components
Bi-directional translation Resultant <-> Components is mandatory

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Force as an Interaction between Bodies

technical_core.canonical_statement: A force is a vector push or pull exerted by one identifiable physical body on another body as a result of an interaction.
technical_core.why_required: Eliminates fictitious forces generated by imagination.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Learner invents internal or non-existent forces.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Every genuine force requires an explicit agent (causer) and receiver (object acted on): F_{on Receiver by Agent}.
technical_core.why_required: Prerequisite for physical realism and Newton's third law.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Drawing force arrows with no physical origin.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Forces are strictly contact forces (requiring physical contact) or field forces (action at a distance).
technical_core.why_required: Guides systematic boundary scanning on FBDs.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Omitting contact forces or inventing contact forces where no bodies touch.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: F_net: vector sum of all external forces on body

representations.name: Interaction Inventory Table
representations.physics_encoded: Explicit table of external boundary interactions
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Explicit Agent and Receiver identities for every force
representations.verification_method: Every force must trace to a real physical body in universe

model_conditions.why_needed: Continuum forces are macroscopic manifestations of electromagnetism

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Identify target object of interest
Scan for field forces (gravity: Earth on object)
Trace boundary perimeter to locate all physical contact points
Verify every candidate force has an identifiable external agent

required_transformations.description: Book on table in elevator -> Gravity (Earth) + Normal (Table)

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: A moving body possesses a force keeping it moving
misconceptions.why_plausible: Pushing an object across carpet requires continuous effort
misconceptions.required_counterexample: Puck gliding on frictionless ice maintains constant velocity with zero forward force
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Forces cause changes in motion (acceleration), not velocity itself

problem_families.name: Interaction Classification
problem_families.recognition_cues: Narrative of physical scene asking to identify all acting forces
problem_families.first_technical_move: Draw boundary around object; scan field forces and boundary contacts
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Adding forward force in direction of motion
problem_families.typical_unknown: Complete table of real physical forces

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Conceptually deep due to Aristotelian misconceptions, mathematically simple

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Force of motion included in force inventory
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Force of motion is fictitious; forces require identifiable external physical agents

technical_core.canonical_statement: A system is isolated by defining an imaginary closed boundary around the body of interest, severing all external connections.
technical_core.why_required: Dictates exactly which forces count as external.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Blurring internal and external forces.

technical_core.canonical_statement: An FBD represents the isolated body showing ALL external forces acting ON that body as directed vectors.
technical_core.why_required: Primary intermediate cognitive bridge from scene to equations.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Bypassing FBD causes omitted forces and sign errors.

technical_core.canonical_statement: An FBD must contain ONLY forces exerted ON the isolated body BY external agents. Forces exerted BY the body are strictly prohibited.
technical_core.why_required: Newton's second law governs acceleration from forces ON the body.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Drawing action and reaction on the same FBD leading to false cancellation.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: Sum of vectors crossing system boundary

representations.name: Free-Body Diagram
representations.physics_encoded: Vector forces acting on isolated system in declared inertial frame
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Central dot, labeled force arrows, coordinate axes
representations.common_incorrect_version: Drawing m*a or velocity as a force on the body dot
representations.verification_method: Count forces on FBD: must match boundary contacts + gravity exactly

model_conditions.why_needed: Lines of action meet at center of mass
model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Extended body requires distributed FBD and torque

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: State exact body being isolated
Draw central dot and downward gravity vector
Trace boundary contact points and draw contact forces
Filter out internal forces and forces exerted BY the body
Draw coordinate axes adjacent to diagram

required_transformations.description: Block on incline with rope -> Dot with gravity, normal, tension, friction

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Draw m*a as a force on the FBD
misconceptions.why_plausible: m*a appears in the equation sum F = ma
misconceptions.required_counterexample: If m*a were a force, then sum F - ma = 0 and nothing could ever accelerate
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: m*a is the kinematic outcome, never a force. Prohibited on the body dot.

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Draw normal force of floor on shoe AND push of shoe on floor on shoe's FBD
misconceptions.why_plausible: Both occur at the same contact interface
misconceptions.required_counterexample: Push on floor acts ON the floor, belongs on floor's FBD
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Filter rule: Does this force act ON the isolated body? If not, discard.

problem_families.name: FBD Construction
problem_families.recognition_cues: Physical setup given requiring equations of motion
problem_families.first_technical_move: Isolate body as dot; replace each contact with vector arrow
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Skipping FBD and guessing equation signs

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: High cognitive load in spatial isolation and filtering out m*a and third-law pairs

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Writing dynamic equations directly without an FBD
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: FBD is non-negotiable prerequisite for equations of motion

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Action-reaction pair drawn on same body's FBD
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Action-reaction pairs act on different bodies, prohibited on same FBD

technical_core.canonical_statement: An object continues at rest or in uniform straight-line motion unless acted upon by a non-zero net external force.
technical_core.why_required: Defines force as the cause of acceleration.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Belief that constant velocity requires forward driving force.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Translational equilibrium is defined as a = 0, physically equivalent to sum(F) = 0. It does NOT mean no forces act.
technical_core.why_required: Prevents confusing equilibrium with lack of interaction.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Stating an object at rest has no forces on it.

representations.name: Closed Force Polygon
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Head-to-tail polygon must return to start point
representations.common_incorrect_version: Open polygon claimed to be in equilibrium
representations.verification_method: Check loop closure: sum of vectors must be zero vector

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Confirm reference frame is inertial
Identify velocity is constant (a = 0)
Draw complete FBD and resolve forces along axes
Set up independent equations: sum F_x = 0, sum F_y = 0

required_transformations.description: Suspended lamp with 2 cables -> 2T sin(theta) - mg = 0

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: An object at rest has no forces acting on it
misconceptions.required_counterexample: Book on table: gravity pulls down 9.8 N, table pushes up 9.8 N. If table removed, book falls.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Equilibrium means vector sum is zero, not absence of forces

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: A car moving at constant 100 km/h has a net forward force
misconceptions.required_counterexample: Engine force balances air drag and friction; net force is strictly zero
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Constant velocity implies a = 0 implies net force = 0

problem_families.name: Static Particle Equilibrium
problem_families.recognition_cues: Suspended object at rest supported by strings or struts
problem_families.first_technical_move: Draw FBD and resolve forces along x and y
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Setting tension equal to weight without angle factors

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Deep misconceptions regarding constant velocity and net force

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Equilibrium described as no forces acting
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Equilibrium requires sum F = 0, not absence of physical interactions

technical_core.canonical_statement: The net external force on a body equals the time rate of change of its linear momentum: F_net = dp/dt.
technical_core.why_required: Fundamental definition of Newton's second law.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Treating F=ma as an unprovable postulate rather than constant-mass rate.

technical_core.canonical_statement: For constant mass, sum F = m*a. Acceleration is directly proportional to net force and points strictly in net force direction.
technical_core.why_required: Operational engine for classical dynamics.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Treating F=ma as scalar arithmetic without directional correspondence.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Vector sum F = m*a decouples into independent equations: sum F_x = m*a_x and sum F_y = m*a_y.
technical_core.why_required: Foundational algorithm for solving 2D dynamics.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Blending vertical forces into horizontal acceleration equations.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: Signed force sum and acceleration along x
Signed force sum and acceleration along y

representations.name: Resolved Axis FBD
representations.physics_encoded: FBD with force components resolved parallel and perpendicular to acceleration
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Replacement of original angled force by resolved components
representations.common_incorrect_version: Leaving angled forces unresolved while writing scalar equations
representations.verification_method: Check dimensions: every force component appears in exactly one axis equation

model_conditions.why_needed: Allows pulling m out of derivative d(mv)/dt
model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Variable mass requires rocket thrust terms

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Isolate body and construct complete FBD
Align +x with acceleration direction and +y perpendicular
Resolve non-aligned forces into components
Write sum F_x = m*a and sum F_y = 0
Solve resulting system for acceleration and contact forces

required_transformations.description: Block sliding down incline -> mg sin(theta) - f_k = ma, N - mg cos(theta) = 0

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Acceleration must point in the direction the object is moving
misconceptions.why_plausible: When speeding up in a straight line, a and v align
misconceptions.required_counterexample: Braking car moves forward (v > 0) but accelerates backward (a < 0)
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Acceleration points in direction of net force, NOT velocity

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Add all forces as scalars and set equal to m*a
misconceptions.why_plausible: In 1D problems scalar arithmetic happens to match
misconceptions.required_counterexample: Pulling wagon at 30 deg: only 100*cos(30) accelerates wagon horizontally

problem_families.name: 2D Incline / Angled Dynamics
problem_families.recognition_cues: Object accelerating on surface under angled forces
problem_families.first_technical_move: Align axes with acceleration; resolve angled forces and weight
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Setting N = mg automatically on inclines or angled pulls
problem_families.typical_unknown: Acceleration a and normal force N

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Concurrently requires FBD construction, 2D vector resolution, axis decoupling, and linear system solving

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Combining forces from perpendicular axes into single scalar sum for ma
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Axis-wise decoupling (sum F_x = ma_x, sum F_y = ma_y) must be enforced

technical_core.canonical_statement: To every action there is always an equal and opposite reaction: F_AB = -F_BA.
technical_core.why_required: Establishes reciprocity of interactions and conservation of momentum.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Belief that stronger body exerts greater force.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Action and reaction forces act strictly on two different bodies; they NEVER act on the same body.
technical_core.why_required: Prevents cancelling action and reaction on one body.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Claiming action and reaction cancel, making acceleration impossible.

technical_core.canonical_statement: An action-reaction pair consists of forces of the exact same physical nature (both gravitational, both normal, etc.).
technical_core.why_required: Prevents pairing normal contact force with gravity.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Claiming normal force on book is reaction to gravity.

mandatory_equations.formula: F_{A on B} = - F_{B on A}
mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: Equal and opposite force vectors on distinct bodies

representations.name: Third-Law Dual FBD
representations.physics_encoded: Two separate FBDs for bodies A and B with reciprocal forces
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Separate drawings for both bodies; pair never on same body
representations.common_incorrect_version: Drawing both F_AB and F_BA attached to body A
representations.verification_method: Check subscripts: F_12 must pair with F_21

model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Finite signal speed requires field momentum

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Identify interacting bodies A and B
Identify force by A on B: F_AB
Apply Newton III: F_BA = -F_AB
Confirm same magnitude, opposite direction, same nature
Place F_AB on FBD of B and F_BA on FBD of A

required_transformations.description: Man pushes crate -> Crate FBD shows forward push; Man FBD shows backward push

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Normal force on book resting on table is third-law reaction to weight
misconceptions.why_plausible: Both forces act on book, equal magnitude (N=mg), opposite directions
misconceptions.required_counterexample: Accelerating lift: N = m(g+a) != mg, yet 3rd law pairs are always equal
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Reaction to Weight is gravitational pull by book on Earth; reaction to Normal is downward push on table

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: If horse and cart pull equally, neither can ever move
misconceptions.why_plausible: Apparent paradox of equal and opposite forces
misconceptions.required_counterexample: Forces act on different bodies: horse moves forward due to ground friction on hooves
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Never add forces on different bodies. Draw isolated FBD for each body.

problem_families.name: Multi-Block Push in Contact
problem_families.recognition_cues: Two blocks in contact pushed by external force
problem_families.first_technical_move: Separate into two isolated FBDs with equal and opposite contact forces
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Claiming block 1 pushes block 2 harder because system accelerates
problem_families.typical_unknown: System acceleration and contact force between blocks

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Exceptional misconception density regarding action-reaction pairs and normal/weight confusion

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Treating normal force and gravity as action-reaction pair
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Normal force and gravity act on same body and have different physical natures

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Normal Contact Force and Surface Constraints

technical_core.canonical_statement: The normal force N is a contact force exerted by a compressed solid surface on a body, directed perpendicular to the surface.
technical_core.why_required: Sets geometric directional invariant of surface contact.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Drawing normal force in a non-perpendicular direction.

technical_core.canonical_statement: The normal force is a constraint force self-adjusting to enforce the kinematic condition a_perp = 0.
technical_core.why_required: Establishes that N has no fixed formula; solved from perpendicular dynamics.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Treating N as a constant property of the body.

technical_core.canonical_statement: N = mg holds ONLY for solitary body at rest on flat horizontal surface. Under any other conditions, N != mg.
technical_core.why_required: Primary defense against substituting N = mg blindly.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Blindly writing N = mg on inclines or angled pulls.

mandatory_equations.formula: sum(F_perp) = m*a_perp = 0 => N = sum(opposing perpendicular force components)
mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: N solved algebraically from perpendicular force balance

representations.name: Surface Normal Diagram
representations.physics_encoded: Perpendicularity of normal force relative to tangent surface
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Perpendicular square indicator; arrow pointing into body
representations.common_incorrect_version: Drawing N pointing straight up toward sky on an incline
representations.verification_method: Check angle with surface tangent: must be exactly 90 deg

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Identify surface contact plane and draw N perpendicular into body
Sum all forces along perpendicular axis
Set sum F_perp = m*a_perp = 0 and solve for N algebraically
Check detachment condition N >= 0

required_transformations.description: Pull at angle theta -> N = mg - F sin(theta)

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: N = mg is the universal formula for normal force
misconceptions.why_plausible: Holds in introductory flat horizontal examples
misconceptions.required_counterexample: Incline: N = mg cos(theta); Angled pull: N = mg - F sin(theta); Elevator: N = m(g+a)
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: There is no general formula for normal force; N is an unknown solved from dynamics

problem_families.name: Normal Force Calculation
problem_families.recognition_cues: Object on surface with angled forces, inclines, or vertical accelerations
problem_families.first_technical_move: Write perpendicular balance sum F_perp = m*a_perp
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Replacing N with mg before writing equations
problem_families.typical_unknown: Normal force N and apparent weight

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Unlearning N = mg; solving constraint force from perpendicular dynamics

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Automatic N = mg assumption on incline or angled pull
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Normal force must be solved from perpendicular dynamic balance

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Tension in Light Strings and Pulley Systems

technical_core.canonical_statement: A flexible string can only pull, never push (T >= 0); tension points away from the body along string line.
technical_core.why_required: Fundamental directional invariant for string contact.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Drawing tension pushing into body.

technical_core.canonical_statement: An ideal string is massless and inextensible; tension is strictly uniform along its continuous length.
technical_core.why_required: F_net = m_s a = 0 implies delta T = 0.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Assigning different tensions to segments of same continuous string.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Because string is inextensible, connected bodies share acceleration magnitude along constraint path: a1 = a2 = a.
technical_core.why_required: Kinematic coupling to close dynamic system.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Treating accelerations of connected blocks as independent unknowns.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: Acceleration of ideal vertical Atwood machine

representations.name: Pulley-String System Diagram
representations.physics_encoded: Multi-body connected system with continuous string geometry
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Tension pulling away from each body along string
representations.common_incorrect_version: Labeling tensions T1 and T2 for same massless string
representations.verification_method: Check continuous segments: must carry identical variable T

model_conditions.why_needed: Uniform tension and rigid acceleration coupling

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Identify continuous strings and assign single tension label T
Draw isolated FBD for each connected body with tension pointing away
Establish kinematic acceleration constraint a1 = a2 = a
Write Newton's second law for each body along motion path
Solve system for acceleration and tension

required_transformations.description: Half Atwood machine -> T = m1 a, m2 g - T = m2 a

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: In an Atwood machine, tension in string equals hanging weight: T = m2 g
misconceptions.required_counterexample: If T = m2 g, net force is zero and hanging mass could never accelerate downward
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: When accelerating downward, T = m2(g - a) < m2 g

problem_families.name: Atwood Pulley Dynamics
problem_families.recognition_cues: Two masses connected by string over a pulley
problem_families.first_technical_move: Draw separate FBDs for each mass; link accelerations
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Setting T = mg on accelerating hanging mass
problem_families.typical_unknown: Acceleration a and string tension T

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Multi-body coupled equations and tension bounds in accelerating systems

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Setting tension equal to mg in an accelerating Atwood machine
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Tension equals mg only in static equilibrium; in downward acceleration T < mg

technical_core.canonical_statement: Static friction prevents relative sliding and is self-adjusting: 0 <= f_s <= f_{s,max} = mu_s * N.
technical_core.why_required: Prevents equating static friction blindly to mu_s * N.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Calculating f_s = 50 N for a block pushed with 5 N, predicting backward acceleration.

technical_core.canonical_statement: During active relative sliding, kinetic friction is f_k = mu_k * N, where mu_k <= mu_s.
technical_core.why_required: Differentiates sliding regime from static threshold.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Using static coefficient during active sliding motion.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Friction opposes relative motion between contact surfaces, NOT motion relative to ground.
technical_core.why_required: Explains how friction provides forward propulsion (walking, car tires).
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Belief that friction always opposes velocity.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: f_s: static friction, mu_s: static coefficient, N: normal force
f_k: kinetic friction, mu_k: kinetic coefficient

representations.name: Friction vs Applied Force Plot
representations.physics_encoded: Piecewise response of friction as applied force increases
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Slope 1 self-adjusting line and sharp drop to kinetic plateau
representations.common_incorrect_version: Flat horizontal line for all applied forces

model_conditions.why_needed: Friction independent of contact area and sliding speed

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Calculate normal force N from perpendicular balance
Calculate static threshold: f_{s,max} = mu_s * N
Compare applied driving force F_drive with f_{s,max}
If F_drive <= f_{s,max}: a = 0, f_s = F_drive. Else: f = f_k = mu_k * N, solve ma

required_transformations.description: 10 kg box, mu_s=0.5, pushed with 30 N -> f_{s,max}=49 N -> a=0, f_s=30 N

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Static friction is always equal to mu_s * N
misconceptions.why_plausible: Formulas memorized as equations rather than inequalities
misconceptions.required_counterexample: Pushing car with 10 N: if f_s = mu_s * N = 7840 N, car would shoot backward!
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Static friction self-adjusts to balance applied force up to mu_s * N ceiling

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Friction always opposes the direction an object moves
misconceptions.why_plausible: Sliding boxes slow down due to friction
misconceptions.required_counterexample: Walking: ground friction pushes forward on foot, propelling person forward
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Friction opposes relative sliding between surfaces, NOT motion relative to ground

problem_families.name: Dry Friction Thresholding
problem_families.recognition_cues: Object on rough surface with applied force
problem_families.first_technical_move: Calculate N; evaluate f_{s,max} = mu_s * N; compare with driving force
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Calculating f = mu_k * N immediately without checking static threshold
problem_families.typical_unknown: Friction regime, actual friction force f, acceleration a

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Branching if/else regime logic, normal force dependency, extreme misconception density

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Static friction calculated blindly as mu_s * N when driving force is below threshold
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Static friction is governed by inequality f_s <= mu_s * N and self-adjusts to balance applied force

technical_core.canonical_statement: A composite system of multiple bodies can be treated as a single mass M_tot = sum(m_i) accelerated by external forces.
technical_core.why_required: Enables fast determination of overall system acceleration.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Learner gets bogged down in simultaneous multi-variable systems.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Internal forces cancel in pairs by Newton III and do not appear in whole-system equation.
technical_core.why_required: Validates system-as-a-whole approach mathematically.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Adding internal tensions to total system external force sums.

technical_core.canonical_statement: String length constraint f(x_1, ..., x_n) = L differentiated twice yields acceleration relations.
technical_core.why_required: Provides necessary kinematic relations to close system of dynamical equations.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Assuming all connected bodies always share identical accelerations.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: External force sum and system acceleration
Virtual work constraint for inextensible string networks

representations.name: Multi-body System Boundary
representations.physics_encoded: System boundary demarcating internal vs external forces
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Explicit dashed boundary line and external force identification
representations.common_incorrect_version: Showing internal tension arrows crossing composite boundary
representations.verification_method: Every force in sum F_ext must have agent outside boundary

model_conditions.why_needed: No relative elastic delay or oscillation

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Formulate string length constraint equation and differentiate twice
Choose strategy: system as whole (for a) vs separate FBDs (for internal forces)
Write Newton's second law for each body along motion direction
Substitute acceleration constraints and solve linear system

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: All objects in any pulley system accelerate at the same rate
misconceptions.required_counterexample: Movable pulley: pulling 2 m of string lifts load 1 m -> a_load = 0.5 * a_rope
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Acceleration ratios must be derived from string length conservation

problem_families.name: Movable Pulley Acceleration
problem_families.recognition_cues: Pulleys that move up and down with the load
problem_families.first_technical_move: Write string length in terms of position coordinates from fixed ceiling
problem_families.typical_unknown: Accelerations of individual masses and string tensions

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Synthesizes multi-FBD tracking, differential constraints, and linear system elimination

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Assuming 1:1 acceleration in movable pulley system without constraint derivation
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Movable pulley systems require kinematic acceleration constraint derivation from string length
